partner_context.their_ambition: Uber Boat by Thames Clippers runs London's river-bus network under the TfL umbrella, with record post-pandemic ridership and a city pushing river transport as relief for a maxed-out Tube and road network.
partner_context.their_pressure: The diesel catamaran fleet is speed-limited, wake constrains operations on the tidal river, the network thins out beyond the central piers, and emissions sit awkwardly with London's net-zero and ULEZ agenda.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling fleet that runs the river bus faster, extends cleanly up- and down-river to new developments and the estuary, throws almost no wake, and decarbonizes the service in line with London's net-zero goals.

hero.title: The Thames, on foils.
hero.subtitle: A faster, cleaner, near-wakeless foiling layer for London's river bus.
hero.what_we_do_together: Uber Boat by Thames Clippers and Transport for London bring the river-bus network, piers and ridership; Navier brings a foiling fleet that runs faster, reaches farther up and down the estuary, and throws almost no wake on the tidal Thames.

why_now: London is actively expanding river transport, the city has aggressive net-zero and air-quality mandates, Thames wake is a live constraint, and river-bus ridership is at record highs — the moment for a foiling layer is now.
multimodal_fit: Londoners already chain Tube, bus, bike and river bus on the same fare rails; a foiling pier slots into the same Oyster/contactless trip — Tube to the pier, foil down the river, onward — adding fast clean water capacity to TfL's network.

journeys_unlocked.today: A diesel river-bus or a packed Jubilee line.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A fast silent zero-wake foiling hop down the river to the Wharf.

journeys_unlocked.today: The full ~90-min length of the river-bus line on diesel cats.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A faster zero-wake foiling run along the length of the tidal Thames.

journeys_unlocked.today: Limited or no direct river service to the new riverside districts.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A clean foiling connection serving London's new riverside developments.

journeys_unlocked.today: No fast river service to the outer estuary.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A clean Quanta-LR hybrid run down the estuary toward the Kent/Essex coast.

differentiation.why_navier: A software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling platform that is faster, longer-range and near-wakeless — extending the river bus up and down the estuary, ending wake constraints, and decarbonizing it with only pier-side changes, on TfL's existing fare rails.

proof_points.claim: London's river bus is at record ridership.
proof_points.evidence: Uber Boat by Thames Clippers carries millions a year, with the city pushing river transport as Tube/road relief.

proof_points.claim: London has aggressive net-zero + air mandates.
proof_points.evidence: Net-zero targets and ULEZ create direct alignment for a zero-emission foiling fleet.
Wake rules limit speeds and operations; near-zero-wake foiling resolves the issue and unlocks new piers.

proof_points.claim: Tube and road capacity is maxed.
proof_points.evidence: With the Tube and roads at capacity, the tidal river is London's most under-used central right-of-way.

objections.concern: The Thames is tidal with strong currents and bridge clearances.
objections.response: Foils handle current and chop; software-defined routing manages tide windows and the central bridges as the existing fleet already does, and Pioneer II's profile clears the spans.

objections.concern: River bus runs on TfL fare integration.
objections.response: Foiling slots straight into the existing Oyster/contactless rails — same fares, faster and cleaner service, no rider re-education.

objections.concern: Procurement runs through TfL / the operator.
objections.response: We start with a demonstration on a flagship segment (central ↔ Canary Wharf, or a wake-sensitive western reach) to prove speed, wake and emissions before any fleet decision.

objections.concern: The estuary is exposed and busy.
objections.response: Quanta-LR hybrid suits estuary distances and conditions; routing manages the commercial Port of London traffic.

phases.narrative: Launch a foiling pilot on the busiest central reach — Embankment/Tower ↔ Canary Wharf — proving faster, near-wakeless river-bus capacity on TfL's fare rails.

the_ask.partner_brings: Thames Clippers / TfL bring the river-bus network, piers, fare integration, ridership and net-zero mandate.
the_ask.together: A faster, cleaner, near-wakeless foiling layer that extends London's river bus up and down the estuary and decarbonizes it.

close.title: London's river, on foils.
close.body: A faster, longer-range, near-wakeless foiling layer for the Thames river bus — extending it up and down the estuary, ending wake constraints, and decarbonizing it on TfL's fare rails.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: London's river-transport expansion, net-zero/ULEZ mandates, tidal-Thames wake constraints, and record river-bus ridership converge — a faster, zero-wake, zero-emission foiling fleet answers all four.
wow_corridors: Central piers ↔ Canary Wharf / Royal Docks (fast)

end_state.headline: The fast, clean, near-wakeless water layer of London transit.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Putney + central piers + Canary Wharf + Royal Docks/Thamesmead + Barking Riverside + the Thames Estuary.
end_state.narrative: A foiling fleet runs London's river bus on TfL's fare rails — faster and near-wakeless through the centre, extended to new riverside developments, and reaching down the estuary — decarbonizing the service in line with London's net-zero goals.
